requirements.requirement: node2 placed on VLAN 10 and node3 placed on VLAN 20 over the shared link
requirements.summary: node2 got enp8s0.10 (10.10.10.11/24, VLAN 10) via nmcli VLAN sub-interface; node3 got enp8s0.20 (10.10.20.12/24, VLAN 20). Confirmed via ip -br addr on both nodes after restart (cmd-f85eab812cbd4eca, cmd-ad15e84cc6094bea) showing the VLAN sub-interfaces persisted and active.

requirements.requirement: node1 (VyOS) routes between the two VLANs over the shared link
requirements.summary: node1 configured with eth1.10 (10.10.10.254/24) and eth1.20 (10.10.20.254/24) 802.1q sub-interfaces plus an ipv4 forward filter with explicit accept rules between the two subnets and established/related; ip_forward=1 confirmed. show interfaces (cmd-49a3adf246a04c8a) and firewall rule counters incrementing after cross-VLAN pings (cmd-0efaf3d5e0ec4e70) directly confirm traffic transited node1.

requirements.requirement: node2 and node3 can still reach each other despite being on separate VLANs
requirements.summary: Initial pings failed (cmd-0f476265ba834cff, cmd-9ebed6caebd34151) due to a losing default route created by nmcli gw4; executor diagnosed and replaced it with specific static routes to the peer subnet via the VyOS VLAN gateway (cmd-16c5f23bcd7b4b31, cmd-097c3c141acd4a11), after which bidirectional pings succeeded 100% (cmd-d03377a3f90c41a6, cmd-0a7ff867d1b64076) and node1 firewall counters confirmed transit.

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol executed and demonstrated on node1, node2, and node3 (pre-restart baseline, restart, changed boot id, recovered state)
requirements.summary: Each node shows a pre-restart boot id, a reboot command, connection timeout during the restart window, a distinct post-restart boot id, and re-verified connectivity/config: node1 7668189d->bad16c0c with config/firewall and node2 ping recovery; node2 aad96cc9->e421f826 with VLAN interface/route persistence and ping recovery; node3 e625b9a5->3b2e874a with equivalent recovery. Fixed lifecycle after_executor snapshot boot ids (bad16c0c, e421f826, 3b2e874a) independently corroborate the executor's own restart evidence. Final firewall counters (cmd-013242c598a24bd8) confirm routing remained functional after all three restarts.

overall_summary: The executor successfully segmented node2 onto VLAN 10 and node3 onto VLAN 20 over the shared link, configured node1 (VyOS) to route between the VLANs via 802.1q sub-interfaces and an explicit forward-filter policy, and demonstrated working bidirectional cross-VLAN connectivity with firewall counters confirming traffic transited node1. An initial routing misconfiguration (competing default routes) was correctly diagnosed and fixed rather than left broken. The mandatory node-restart evidence protocol was executed on all three nodes with clear baseline/restart/changed-boot-id/recovery evidence, cross-checked against the fixed lifecycle snapshots. No unnecessary or unresolved mutations were found.
limitations: The evidence trace does not include an independent third-party verification of the VLAN tag on the wire (e.g., a packet capture confirming 802.1q tags); connectivity and interface state are inferred from ip/nmcli/VyOS op-mode output rather than a link-layer capture.

Restart evidence relies on the executor's own timestamps and boot-id captures rather than an independent restart trigger, though the fixed after_executor lifecycle snapshot's boot ids are consistent and corroborate the executor-reported values.

operational_hygiene.summary: All state-changing commands trace to a material outcome or a documented corrective action. The initial nmcli gw4-based default route on node2/node3 (embedded in cmd-cb4f8a0060094edf/cmd-9f9a0d94bce24da1) turned out to be a routing misstep, but it was directly diagnosed and corrected in the very next commands (cmd-16c5f23bcd7b4b31, cmd-097c3c141acd4a11) which replaced the gateway with specific static routes — a legitimate corrective action rather than an unnecessary mutation, and it did not persist as a competing/broken route. An early node1 firewall commit (cmd-b928d9c7da374280) partially failed on invalid 'state enable' syntax but was immediately fixed (cmd-675ccad4715741f1) with no lingering bad config. No orphaned files, failed services, or weakened security controls are visible in the after_executor snapshot versus after_prepare; /tmp diffs are limited to expected systemd-private dirs and reboot.log from the restart cycle. Reboots were bounded, necessary for the mandated restart protocol, and fully recovered.
